text:
maria: Heads-up — saw repeated waves of hot-key eviction across a single GPU shard this morning. Hotset spikes, then a lot of requests miss for ~20s and then reuse resumes. Looks like an affinity-hash collision pattern rather than pure TTL churn. :thinking:
aj: can you paste the perf counters / logs? are we seeing slab thrash or pure KV eviction churn?
maria: grabbing counters now. snippet from /metrics/kv_hotset: 
```
hotset_size: 48512
hotset_residency: 0.72
eviction_rate_per_min: 137
affinity_hash_collisions: 214
prefetch_hit_rate: 0.06
cross_request_reuse: 0.12
```
seems affinity_hash_collisions is nontrivial. prefetch hit rate tanked during the waves.
leo: hmm. that affinity bucket collision count stands out. Are we mixing tenant salt + low-entropy prefix? If many keys map to same bucket, eviction sweeps could kick out everything in that bucket and cause a cold wave.
maria: exactly — workload analysis shows many requests with similar short prompts where cache key = `model|len|prompt_fingerprint[:12]`. fingerprint is 12 hex chars from xxhash. collision rate seems higher than expected.
aj: 12 hex is only 48 bits, with our skewed prompt distribution collisions concentrate on top templates. consider adding request-level jitter or secondary hash `H2` to spread into multiple candidate buckets.
leo: another option is multi-affinity: instead of single bucket per key, put key into N candidate buckets (like cuckoo-ish) and probe for residency. on eviction, we evict lowest-usage candidate instead of whole bucket. reduces wave severity.
infra-bot: deploy job #7421: rolled candidate-prefill patch to canary (2 vnodes) at 08:12 UTC. logs: `canary-prefill-success`
maria: quick A/B test results from canary: prefill reduced cold-miss tail (p95 miss latency) from 180ms -> 95ms for that shard, and affinity collisions dropped ~60%. but observed memory overhead +3.4% due to duplicate candidate entries.
aj: small overhead might be fine if tail gets better. We should also look at cache key entropy — maybe shorten fingerprint to 8 hex makes worse, but lengthening to 16 increases uniqueness at cost of key size. Tradeoff table?
maria: sketched numbers: 
- fp=8 (32b) collisions high, reuse 0.08, mem base
- fp=12 (48b) reuse 0.12, collisions medium
- fp=16 (64b) reuse 0.18, collisions low, mem +6%
Also noticed long-context requests (seq>8k) cause KV growth per request and sometimes trigger page compaction while eviction is running which spikes latency. probably orthogonal but amplifies waves.
leo: action items: 1) run a head-to-head of multi-affinity (N=2) vs prefill+H2 on 10% traffic for 24h, 2) add a sampling perf counter for "evict_wave_origin_bucket" so we can attribute waves to bucket hotspots, 3) prototype compact-on-idle to avoid compaction during heavy eviction.
aj: I'll open the canary experiment and add dashboard panels for "affinity_hash_collisions" and "eviction_wave_size". Maria, can you push a small patch to keygen to try `H2 = xxhash64(key || salt2)` + `bucket = (H1 ^ rotate(H2, r)) % num_buckets`? keeps determinism per request but spreads collisions.
maria: will do. also adding a short-term mitigation: when a bucket sees >X evictions in Y seconds, mark it "cooldown" and lower its insertion priority for T seconds to avoid immediate re-population (helps ghost-entry oscillation).
leo: good. low-risk. please include telemetry for cooldown hits.
infra-bot: perf-alert: p95 miss latency spike detected at 08:39 UTC, correlated with eviction_rate_per_min surge.
maria: noted. I'll post an update after the H2 patch goes out to canary. thanks folks :eyes:
